name: Cyan, Vengeful Samurai
oracle_text:
This spell costs {1} less to cast for each creature card in your graveyard.
Double strike
Whenever one or more creature cards leave your graveyard, put a +1/+1 counter on Cyan.
blocked_sentences: This spell costs {1} less to cast for each creature card in your graveyard.
Whenever one or more creature cards leave your graveyard, put a +1/+1 counter on Cyan.

needs.what: a self cost reduction whose 'for each' filter may count cards in the caster's graveyard -- i.e. add 'graveyard' to the zones a cost reduction filter may name, and let the counting walk that zone at pricing time the way it already walks the battlefield and command zone
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The only two reduction languages are the card-level 'cost_reduction' / cost 'mana_reduction' (reference cost_keys 'mana_reduction') and the battlefield static 'spell_cost_reduction'. The former's counting filter is restricted to COST_REDUCTION_ZONES = {battlefield, command}, so a graveyard filter is a load error rather than a silent zero; the latter is a battlefield static that discounts a *different* card and its magnitude comes from static_value_keys, whose 'count' is filtered by static_filter_keys -- a set with no 'zone' key at all, so it cannot be scoped to a graveyard either. There is no third place a spell's own price can be lowered from.

needs.what: a trigger event fired when one or more cards leave a specified player's graveyard, batched so that a single move of several cards fires the ability once, and filterable by the leaving cards' printed characteristics (here: creature cards, your graveyard)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: trigger_events has 'leaves_battlefield' and 'dies', which watch the battlefield and fire on cards arriving in a graveyard rather than departing it; 'discard' and 'sacrificed' likewise only ever put cards *into* a graveyard. Nothing in the list observes the graveyard as a source zone, so the many ways a card leaves it -- reanimation via return_from_graveyard or put_onto_battlefield, exile via the exile op or an exile_from_graveyard cost, a graveyard cast, a shuffle-back -- all happen unobserved. The batching ('one or more ... leave') is a second requirement no existing event carries: every listed event fires per object.
